bullets: Nasdaq futures -2.2%, S&P -1% after Amazon (-7%) and Intel (-26%) earnings reignite AI-capex spending fears; chip names AMD/NVDA/AVGO also down.
Asia mixed overnight: Nikkei -2.6%, Kospi -4.7%, Hang Seng +1.6%; Europe's Stoxx 600 -0.3% despite stronger euro-area growth data.
VIX +7.7% to 18.5 signals rising risk-off tone; Brent oil +2.7% on Chevron/Exxon refining beats, yields and dollar softer.

CRM.why: Drop tracked a sector-wide SaaS selloff after ServiceNow's contract-growth slowdown spooked enterprise-software investors broadly (Workday -5%, Datadog -5.7%); no Salesforce-specific bad news found; its own analyst moves were PT-raises.
CRM.bull: Drop was sector-wide SaaS fear from ServiceNow's outlook, not Salesforce-specific damage, and shares look undervalued at current levels.
CRM.bear: Enterprise software demand worries are real and sentiment-driven, which can cap a quick bounce even without company bad news.

GDDY.why: GDDY beat Q3 estimates and guided to the high end of FY revenue, but fell on the earnings call itself: management flagged Airo's lower gross margins from inference costs, revenue-cannibalization risk, and competitive pricing pressure; a shareholder-lawsuit alert also surfaced.
GDDY.bull: GDDY beat Q3 estimates, hit the high end of revenue guidance, and Airo's bookings run-rate doubled past $100M.
GDDY.bear: Stock fell on earnings day itself on margin and cannibalization concerns around Airo, a company-specific reassessment, not a sector move.
flags: beat but sold on margin quality

MOH.why: Q3 beat on revenue/EPS hid a 52% GAAP net-income drop on Medicaid margin squeeze and membership losses; four analysts (JPM, UBS, MS, RBC) cut ratings to Neutral/Equal-weight on fundamentals, and 2027 premium guidance was trimmed. Health sector overall was up, so this is company damage, not sector weakness.
MOH.bull: 2026 EPS guidance was reaffirmed and management sees 2027 EPS building blocks above $9.50 as Florida CMS ramps.
MOH.bear: Net income fell 52% on margin squeeze, membership losses continue, and four analysts cut ratings to Neutral on fundamentals.

WEX.why: WEX beat Q3 estimates on all lines and raised FY2026 EPS/revenue guidance, yet the stock barely reacted positively and has pulled back from a recent 33% rally; one Morgan Stanley downgrade (Oct 27, PT raised) preceded earnings. No clear damage found, but the muted reaction to a clean beat is unexplained.
WEX.bull: WEX beat Q3 estimates on every line and raised full-year EPS and revenue guidance, a fundamentally strong quarter.
WEX.bear: Despite the beat, the stock barely moved higher after a big prior rally, and one analyst downgraded shares just before earnings.

ADP.why: ADP beat Q1 estimates and raised FY27 revenue/EPS growth guidance; the sell-off was a 'sell-the-news' valuation reset (unchanged margin-expansion target, softer NER Pulse hiring data) amid a broad market risk-off day driven by Amazon/Intel AI-capex fears, not ADP-specific damage. Analyst moves kept PTs flat-to-higher.
ADP.bull: ADP beat Q1 estimates and raised FY27 revenue and EPS growth guidance; Stifel reiterated a Buy with PT raised to $305.
ADP.bear: Margin-expansion guidance was left unchanged and ADP's own payroll data show hiring cooling, a headwind for future volume growth.
